findings.claim: The central decision to defer is still resting on an untested compatibility assumption, despite being reframed as conditional.
findings.evidence: Decision says: "Do not adopt MCP `2026-07-28` now" and then narrows the honest form to "defer *given* backward compatibility holds" while also stating "No live 2026-07-28 server was contacted; falsifier 1 is un-run, not passed" and assumption says "Servers keep accepting 2025-03-26 and 2025-06-18... not exercised against a live 2026-07-28 server."
findings.suggested_fix: Do not commit the defer decision as valid until compatibility is exercised, or explicitly change the decision to a temporary unblock with a hard stop before any dependent MCP functionality is relied on.

findings.claim: Falsifier 1 is not practically scheduled, so the highest-risk assumption can remain untested while the defer decision proceeds.
findings.evidence: Falsifier 1 says: "Test: exercise both clients against a live 2026-07-28 server" but gives no deadline, owner, server identity, or fallback if no such live server is available; the decision says this is merely "the first task of the convergence phase."
findings.suggested_fix: Bind falsifier 1 to the same deadline as falsifier 3, name the server or fixture to be used, and define failure if no test environment exists by that date.

findings.claim: The "deferring is free" falsifier uses an arbitrary and incomplete threshold that can miss real deferral cost.
findings.evidence: Falsifier 3 declares failure only on "A sixth version or a sixth consumer" or if "no convergence phase started" by the deadline, but the document gives no source for why six is the failure threshold and does not treat unresolved five-version divergence, broken interoperability, or a started-but-not-completed convergence phase as failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Define success/failure around completed convergence or verified compatibility by the deadline, not only growth from five to six versions/consumers.

findings.claim: The decision record is malformed and the prior-decision check is unreliable, so the document cannot support its own claim that there is no settled ground being re-decided.
findings.evidence: prior_decisions reports: "skipping malformed entry path=.../decision-defer-mcp-2026-07-28-adoption.md err=frontmatter parse error: yaml parse: mapping values are not allowed in this context at line 4 column 16"; the decision frontmatter has an unquoted title containing a colon: "title: Decision: defer MCP 2026-07-28 adoption; converge rmcp in a dedicated phase".
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the frontmatter title and rerun the prior-decision lookup after malformed decision entries are parseable.

findings.file: What was re-measured at write time / Alternatives considered
findings.claim: The decision treats compile success as enough to unblock the parent while admitting that the affected MCP behavior is not tested end to end.
findings.evidence: Decision claims the parent is unblocked based on "`cargo check --lib` clean and `cargo test --lib provenance` 8/8 from cold," but also says "No live 2026-07-28 server was contacted," "ContentBlock as Content is compile-verified only," and rejects protocol-side adoption because there is "no end-to-end MCP test in this stack to catch the regression."
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a minimal end-to-end MCP smoke test before declaring the parent unblocked, or narrow the unblock claim to compilation/provenance only and mark functional MCP behavior as blocked.
